description:
Drift check in BOTH directions before the epic closes:
- Everything plan/phase-1-foundation.md specifies exists in the tree (no silently-descoped task).
- Everything phase 1 built is accounted for in the plan or the decision record (no undocumented subsystem).
- CLAUDE.md's Architecture Decisions summary and plan/module-decisions.md still describe what was actually built -- in particular the internal/platform five (hexfmt, statehash, snapcodec, instrument, clock) and the inward-pointing package boundaries.
- The package layout phase 1a's ARCH-LAYER-1 will police (internal/platform importing nothing from internal/{cpu,device,broadcast,web}) actually holds NOW, so phase 1a arms a rule against a conforming tree rather than a migration.

Conformance PROBES themselves are phase 1a (epic gort-87m); this gate only proves the tree is ready for them and that the record matches the code.

agent: lead

title: GATE: phase 1 verified against the RUNNING stack, on the REAL firmware
description:
Not a suite. The binary is built and RUN on this machine, against the real, uncurated firmware images in firmware/ (FLASH_U202.bin, FLASH_U203.bin) -- not a fixture, not a synthesised ROM.

Close only when ALL of these have been OBSERVED, each with the command and its output quoted in the close reason:
1. ./ctl.sh up (or the documented run command) starts the binary and the health endpoint answers.
2. The firmware loader loads the REAL 2 MB flash images and verifies them against firmware/MANIFEST.md checksums. A deliberately corrupted copy is REFUSED, naming the mismatch.
3. A real checkpoint stream is emitted from a real run -- a non-empty file with a plausible checkpoint count -- and oraclecmp reports agreement/divergence over it, NOT over an empty or truncated stream.
4. The boot gate has been SEEN to go red against a deliberately broken build, and green again afterwards.
5. Developer surfaces (health/instrument endpoints) are confirmed bound to 127.0.0.1 and NOT reachable on the host's LAN address -- checked with a real connection attempt, not by reading the source.

Assert the OUTCOME, never the absence of an exception. A clean exit code over an empty artefact is the failure mode this gate exists to catch.

title: GATE: every test-plan case in phase 1 proved, with an artefact named
description:
Every case in plan/test-plan-phase-1.md is [x], [!] or [?] with the reason it could not run, and every [x] names the artefact that proves it.

PROOF METHOD -- this is what counts, and it is written here rather than only in a dispatch message because the dispatcher forgets:
- The proof is a COMMITTED GO TEST that re-runs. Not a transcript, not a manual observation, not 'the code clearly does this'.
- Pick the layer the case lives in: a unit test for a contract (TC-1.2 snapshot round-trip, TC-1.3 memory aliases, TC-1.8 platform primitives), an integration test for a boot-path behaviour (TC-1.4 wrong ROM refused, TC-1.9 missing variable refuses), a script/exit-code assertion for a gate (TC-1.7 boot gate goes red).
- Several cases demand a NEGATIVE CONTROL and are not proved without it. TC-1.2: a device that forgets a field must FAIL the round-trip test -- add one deliberately and watch it fail. TC-1.6: over an empty or truncated stream the comparison must report a HARNESS FAILURE, not success. TC-1.8: a lower-cased hexfmt key must fail the lookup test; an absent instrument subject must return a harness failure, never a count of zero. TC-1.7: the gate must be SEEN red. Watch each one fail on purpose, then put it back.
- Each tick names its artefact: '- [x] **TC-1.x: ...** (proved: internal/foo/foo_test.go::TestName)'. A tick with no named artefact cannot be audited by anyone who was not in the room.
- A case that genuinely cannot run is [?] with the blocker stated. Never [x] because a commit message mentions the TC id.

A phase epic must not close over unticked cases. The predecessor closed a phase with 9 of 20 proved because the QA issue's description named only the first nine and the remaining eleven belonged to no issue at all -- this issue is what makes the whole set visible at the moment it is due.
